title: Impact of a concurrent multimodal prehabilitation program on functional status, quality of life and surgical outcome in patients undergoing neoadjuvant treatment for resectable non-small cell lung cancer
summary:
Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a malignant neoplasm of abnormal cells in the lungs and one of the most common forms of cancer in humans. Both surgery and drug therapy are associated with considerable physical and psychological stress. Approaches are needed which, in addition to treating the actual tumour, also promote physical and mental health in order to optimise therapy, reduce complications and improve quality of life. 
The planned study is concerned with improving therapy through a pre-treatment programme (prehabilitation) that better prepares patients for the upcoming operation and further therapy. At the same time as neoadjuvant drug treatment (usually 3-4 cycles, i.e. 9-12 weeks before surgery, usually consisting of chemotherapy and immunotherapy), the prehabilitation programme will be carried out over a period of at least 4-6 weeks. The prehabilitation programme is based on a trimodal approach consisting of a physical exercise programme, nutritional and psychological assessment and possible intervention.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name:
Preoperative: multimodal prehabilitation programme (physical exercise programme, nutritional and psychological assessment and possible intervention)
Baseline and 3 follow ups: various questionnaires & cardiopulmonary exercise test

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Age of majority is required, no upper age limit
2.	Resectable Non-Small Cell lung Cancer Stage II-IIIB
3.	indication for neoadjuvant treatment (Chemo alone, Chemo-IO, with or without radiation therapy)
4.	Willingness and ability to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations including follow-up
Exclusion criteria:
none
